text:
maria: Starting the release window now. We're applying the TF change that splits the app service account into two roles (read-only + write) and enables ephemeral creds for CI. Expect a ~7m apply. tagging @cheng @karthik for rollout + rollback plan. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
cheng: thanks. quick Q — does the plan change any bucket policies or KMS key grants? want to confirm secrets access won't break CD pipelines.
maria: plan updates two iam_role resources and adds a new aws_iam_role_policy_attachment for kms-decrypt. No bucket ACL changes. CI will get short-lived creds via sts:AssumeRole + GetSessionToken flow.
olivia: left a quick preflight checklist: `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` then `terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq .` to scan for iam changes. Also run `./scripts/check-ci-keys.sh` to ensure pipeline can assume the new role.
maria: exact commands we ran in staging: ```bash
TF_WORKSPACE=staging terraform init -input=false
TF_WORKSPACE=staging terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
terraform apply -auto-approve plan.tfplan
```
deploybot: deploy queued by maria for env=prod, plan_id=plan-2025-06-05-01, eta ~7m. Logs will stream here.
srebot: preflight checks OK — no dangling policies, kms policy changes scoped to aliases/infra-app-key.
cheng: if the assume-role path fails, do we have fallback to the previous monolithic role?
maria: yes. fallback playbook: 1) abort apply if mid-apply and run `terraform state rollback` (manual) 2) reattach old role binding: `aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name app-monolith --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::123:policy/app-full` 3) redeploy CI env vars pointing to legacy role. I've pasted the commands in ops-runbook.
karthik: adding an escape hatch for ephemeral creds: CI will now attempt ephemeral, then fall back to static cross-account creds for 30s before failing. Config in `ci/cred-fallback.yaml` is already in the repo.
maria: starting apply now. will monitor deploybot and traces.
deploybot: apply started at 2025-06-05T01:12:05Z, plan_id=plan-2025-06-05-01
deploybot: 01:14:10Z - created aws_iam_role.app-readonly
deploybot: 01:14:43Z - created aws_iam_role.app-writer
deploybot: 01:15:05Z - attached policy kms-decrypt to app-writer
deploybot: 01:15:40Z - ERROR: CI assume-role failing with AccessDenied on sts:AssumeRole for arn:aws:iam::123:role/app-writer
maria: seeing the same in staging logs — looks like we missed a trust relationship update in the terraform template for service principals. pausing apply.
cheng: rolling back the last step (detach kms attach and delete app-writer)? prefer to re-add trust and retry if quick. which is faster?
maria: safer to rollback the writer role creation and keep readonly. will run `terraform apply -target=aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.kms_detach -destroy` then `terraform apply -refresh=false` to prune. I'm running now.
karthik: I can hotfix the trust relationship in the role resource and push a tiny plan — but that needs a fresh plan and another apply window.
maria: rollback apply in progress. if succeed, we'll restore CI to use old monolith until next window.
deploybot: rollback apply started at 01:17:02Z
deploybot: 01:17:35Z - destroyed aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.kms-decrypt
deploybot: 01:18:02Z - destroyed aws_iam_role.app-writer
deploybot: 01:18:20Z - rollback complete, state back to pre-change.
srebot: post-rollback checks: bucket access unaffected, KMS grants intact for monolith role. CI pipelines requeued successfully.
maria: thanks all. action items: (1) I will open a follow-up PR to fix trust_policy for app-writer and add an automated smoke test for sts:AssumeRole (2) @karthik please coordinate a 30-min follow-up apply window tomorrow morning to retry with trust fix (3) @cheng add a note in release notes about the staged role migration + rollback that occurred. :white_check_mark:
olivia: added CI smoke test to the infra-e2e job and a test that attempts assume-role for 3s.
cheng: will update release notes and include rollback blurb + impact none on S3 reads/writes.
maria: closing thread, will file the postmortem-lite in #postmortems with timeline. :thumbsup:
